metadata.authorization: Generic public design prior authored without closed-submission data.
metadata.weight_policy: Authored design weights only: 4 primary, 3 common alternative, 2 meaningful secondary, 1 niche legitimate; not empirical usage.

sources.description: Public TUGS format, legal roster, Patch 1 and Patch 1.2 mechanics, and current gen9tugs server data.
Explicitly public generic archetype design judgment based only on public format facts and base-game mechanics.

metadata.rationale: Soundproof and Leftovers support repeated entry; hazards, poison, Defense-based damage, and Parting Shot compress support roles.
metadata.distinguishing_evidence: Soundproof immunity, Leftovers recovery, or any of Stealth Rock, Toxic, and Parting Shot separates it from the setup and Sturdy lines.
metadata.weight_reason: Primary broadly useful Bastiodon support role.

metadata.rationale: ChestoRest gives one reliable reset while Iron Defense powers Body Press; Rock Blast prevents total passivity into Ghost targets.
metadata.distinguishing_evidence: Iron Defense or Chesto Berry is decisive evidence; Rest and Rock Blast further distinguish the set.
metadata.weight_reason: Meaningful secondary win-condition role with narrower matchups.

metadata.rationale: Minimum Speed supports Metal Burst; Sturdy guarantees a full-HP survival and Custap enables emergency hazards, damage, or pivoting afterward.
metadata.distinguishing_evidence: Sturdy, Custap Berry, Metal Burst, or minimum-Speed ordering identifies this niche line.
metadata.weight_reason: Niche but coherent emergency line, kept at the lowest prior.

metadata.rationale: Levitate supplies a Ground immunity while Leftovers, dual STAB, Toxic, and Rapid Spin support a special wall and remover role.
metadata.distinguishing_evidence: Levitate activation, Psychic, Toxic, or passive Leftovers recovery distinguishes it from Regenerator pivoting and Trick Room.
metadata.weight_reason: Common alternative that emphasizes immunity and special durability.

metadata.rationale: Regenerator, Boots, Rapid Spin, Stealth Rock, and Teleport support repeated physical-wall entries and slow momentum.
metadata.distinguishing_evidence: Regenerator healing, Boots hazard behavior, Teleport, or Stealth Rock identifies the pivot package.
metadata.weight_reason: Primary role because it uniquely combines public Regenerator with hazard control and pivoting.

metadata.rationale: Mental Herb protects setup, minimum Speed exploits the public six-turn room, and Teleport passes turns safely to a slow attacker.
metadata.distinguishing_evidence: Trick Room, Mental Herb, Ice Beam, or minimum-Speed ordering distinguishes it immediately.
metadata.weight_reason: Meaningful secondary mode enabler, but less universally applicable than utility sets.

metadata.rationale: Rocky Helmet plus Rough Skin punishes contact; Crag Mend sustains the current 85-HP physical wall while Glare, phazing, and rocks create progress.
metadata.distinguishing_evidence: Crag Mend, Glare, Dragon Tail, Rocky Helmet recoil, or Rough Skin reveals the durable utility package.
metadata.weight_reason: Primary role because it most directly uses Druddigon's public durability upgrade and custom recovery.

metadata.rationale: Life Orb and Sheer Force amplify three secondary-effect coverage moves while Dragon Claw preserves reliable STAB; maximum Speed avoids a fabricated creep benchmark.
metadata.distinguishing_evidence: Life Orb recoil behavior, Sheer Force suppression of secondary effects, or the coverage moves separates it from defensive and slow Band sets.
metadata.weight_reason: Common offensive alternative with broad generic coverage.

metadata.rationale: Choice Band, Mold Breaker, maximum bulk and Attack, and minimum Speed form a strong Trick Room beneficiary with priority outside the room.
metadata.distinguishing_evidence: Choice locking, Mold Breaker messages, Outrage, Sucker Punch, or minimum-Speed ordering distinguishes it.
metadata.weight_reason: Meaningful secondary slow-breaking mode, less flexible than Life Orb.

metadata.rationale: Levitate and Boots minimize hazard pressure while Roost, Defog, U-turn, and public Corrosive Gas provide repeatable removal and item disruption.
metadata.distinguishing_evidence: Levitate, Boots hazard behavior, U-turn, Defog, or Corrosive Gas identifies this package.
metadata.weight_reason: Primary role because it exercises Dustox's new ability and move while preserving removal and momentum.

metadata.rationale: Shield Dust blocks secondary effects; Black Sludge and Roost sustain Toxic and Whirlwind cycling, while Bug Buzz prevents complete passivity.
metadata.distinguishing_evidence: Shield Dust effect blocking, Black Sludge, Toxic, Whirlwind, or Bug Buzz separates it from the Levitate remover.
metadata.weight_reason: Common alternative with a materially different defensive axis and no invented third permutation.

metadata.rationale: Overcoat protects utility from powder and weather chip; Boots, Spikes, Spin, Volt Switch, and minimum-Speed Gyro Ball support repeated slow pivoting.
metadata.distinguishing_evidence: Overcoat, Spikes, Gyro Ball, Boots behavior, or very slow Volt Switch distinguishes this line.
metadata.weight_reason: Primary deliberately approved hazard-removal and pivot role.

metadata.rationale: Sturdy secures emergency action, Leftovers helps restore it, and Defense investment supports Body Press alongside rocks, Spin, and slow pivoting.
metadata.distinguishing_evidence: Sturdy activation, Leftovers, Stealth Rock, or Body Press distinguishes it from Spikes and offensive Custap lines.
metadata.weight_reason: Common alternative with different hazard, ability, and damage choices.

metadata.rationale: Sturdy and Custap support a final action; Toxic Spikes, maximum-Attack Explosion, Spin, and minimum-Speed Gyro Ball create a coherent lead package.
metadata.distinguishing_evidence: Toxic Spikes, Custap Berry, Explosion, or Attack investment reveals the line.
metadata.weight_reason: Niche legitimate lead, intentionally downweighted to avoid excessive hazard permutations.

metadata.rationale: Ancient Shell's public super-effective reduction and physical bulk improve trapping longevity; Whirlpool, Perish Song, Protect, and Freeze-Dry form one coherent plan.
metadata.distinguishing_evidence: Whirlpool, Perish Song, Protect, physical bulk, or Leftovers distinguishes it from pivot and RestTalk lines.
metadata.weight_reason: Meaningful secondary control role with narrower execution requirements.

metadata.rationale: Ancient Shell reduces super-effective damage, Boots preserve entry health, dual STAB pressures targets, Chilly Reception pivots, and Heal Bell supplies team utility.
metadata.distinguishing_evidence: Ancient Shell damage, Boots behavior, Chilly Reception, or Heal Bell identifies the role.
metadata.weight_reason: Primary role because it directly uses both public Lapras additions in a broadly useful package.

metadata.rationale: Water Absorb trades Ancient Shell mitigation for a Water immunity; Leftovers plus RestTalk provides long-duration status absorption with dual STAB.
metadata.distinguishing_evidence: Water Absorb healing, Rest, Sleep Talk, or lack of Ancient Shell distinguishes this tank.
metadata.weight_reason: Common alternative representing a public base ability and different recovery model.

metadata.rationale: Closing Jaws can intercept a manual switch with the selected damaging move; Band, dual STAB, Knock Off, and priority make each selection consequential.
metadata.distinguishing_evidence: Choice locking and the first revealed attack distinguish it; Sucker Punch failure on a switch remains public mechanic evidence, not a successful intercept.
metadata.weight_reason: Primary direct-attacking expression of Mawile's only legal ability.

metadata.rationale: Expert Belt avoids choice locking; Brave preserves both offenses, maximum mixed investment and minimum Speed create a Trick Room-oriented attacker, and Flamethrower broadens interception choices.
metadata.distinguishing_evidence: Flamethrower damage, Expert Belt behavior, mixed damage, or minimum-Speed ordering separates it from physical lines.
metadata.weight_reason: Meaningful secondary coverage line; downweighted because mixed investment is less generally durable.

metadata.rationale: Life Orb supplies flexible power; Swords Dance creates a setup route while Play Rough, Knock Off, and Sucker Punch retain switch-interception choices when an attack is selected.
metadata.distinguishing_evidence: Swords Dance, Life Orb recoil, and lack of choice lock distinguish it from Band and mixed coverage.
metadata.weight_reason: Common alternative because setup changes play materially without inventing a new ability or marginal permutation.

metadata.rationale: Eviolite and Recover preserve bulk while Download and maximum Special Attack power reliable STAB and broad BoltBeam coverage.
metadata.distinguishing_evidence: Download boost, Modest damage, Thunderbolt, or the absence of Trick Room and status separates it.
metadata.weight_reason: Common offensive alternative with a clear public role.

metadata.rationale: Trace creates matchup-dependent public information; Eviolite, Recover, Toxic, paralysis chance, and target-Attack-based Foul Play support a low-investment wall.
metadata.distinguishing_evidence: The copied ability, Toxic, Discharge paralysis, or Foul Play identifies the utility package.
metadata.weight_reason: Primary broadly useful defensive role and the clearest contrast to unsupported National Dex marginals.

metadata.rationale: Quiet maximum Special Attack and minimum Speed exploit the public six-turn room; Eviolite and Recover improve repeat setup while Download supplies pressure.
metadata.distinguishing_evidence: Trick Room, minimum-Speed ordering, or Quiet damage distinguishes it from the faster Download attacker.
metadata.weight_reason: Meaningful secondary mode setter, less universal than the wall and attacker.
